hypothesis: H001: Replacing the 4x-unrolled byte reject inside the string-skip loop of LineIndex.build (src/indexer/lineIndex.ts L256-282 on improve/lineindex_build_throughput 1d2377e) with an aligned Uint32Array word-wise reject loop that tests each byte lane > 0x5c (via ((x & 0xff) <= 0x5c) || ((x >>> 8 & 0xff) <= 0x5c) || ((x >>> 16 & 0xff) <= 0x5c) || ((x >>> 24) <= 0x5c)) will raise the sealed speedup from 1.623 to ~1.75 (~1.08x relative), because it checks 4 string bytes per typed-array load with one combined branch instead of 4 loads and 4 compares, while preserving the exact '> 0x5c' semantics of the merged code so the byte tail is unchanged. This is the lower-variance alternative to swarU32 (idea 1): same u32 structure and alignment guard but simpler lane-wise test instead of haszero, confirmed at median ~1.08x relative (1.077/1.080/1.060/1.114 across 4 passes) with lower variance (1.06-1.11 vs swarU32's 1.11-1.17). Single change: string branch only; outer skip, checkpoint logic, record pushes and for-await loop stay untouched.

steps.change: At the start of each chunk (inside `for await (const raw of handle)`), after `const buf = raw instanceof Buffer ? raw : Buffer.from(raw);` and before the main for-loop, add per-chunk u32 setup: `const base = buf.byteOffset; const aOff = (base + 3) & ~3; const wN = base + n > aOff ? (base + n - aOff) >> 2 : 0; const u32 = new Uint32Array(buf.buffer, aOff, wN);` These locals compute the aligned word range: aOff is the first 4-byte-aligned offset >= base, wN is the word count from aOff to base+n.

Inside the `if (inString)` branch (L256-282), replace the existing 4x-unrolled `while` loop body (L263-270: `if (buf[i] <= 0x5c) break; if (buf[i + 1] <= 0x5c) { i++; break; } ... i += 4;`) with the aligned u32 word loop: `if (((base + i) & 3) === 0) { let w = (base + i - aOff) >> 2; while (w < wN) { const x = u32[w]; if (((x & 0xff) <= 0x5c) || ((x >>> 8 & 0xff) <= 0x5c) || ((x >>> 16 & 0xff) <= 0x5c) || ((x >>> 24) <= 0x5c)) break; w++; } i = aOff - base + (w << 2); }` Keep the existing byte tail loop (`while (i < n) { if (buf[i] <= 0x5c) break; i++; }`) unchanged below it. The alignment guard `((base + i) & 3) === 0` ensures the word loop starts at a 4-byte boundary; unaligned starts fall through to the byte tail, which walks to the next aligned word on its own.

Leave the escaped-carry branch (L272-281: `if (buf[i] === 0x5c) { ... }`), the byte tail after the word loop, and all other branches (outside-string switch, WCLS skip, checkpoint modulo, record pushes, for-await loop, Buffer.from conversion, EOF handling) completely untouched. This is a single-change plan: only the string-skip loop fast path is modified.

expected_outcome.rationale: The scratch harness measured rej4u32 at median ~1.08x relative to the reference across 4 paired passes (1.077/1.080/1.060/1.114), with lower variance than swarU32 (1.06-1.11 vs 1.11-1.17). Expected sealed score 1.623 × 1.08 ≈ 1.75. The word-wise reject keeps the merged code's '> 0x5c' semantics (stops on any byte <= 0x5c, not just quote/backslash), so the existing byte tail handling and escaped-carry branch are unchanged. Correctness confirmed on all sealed edge fixtures plus extras (trailing backslash at EOF, escaped-quote runs, unicode/emoji, leading empty lines, raw newlines inside strings), splits whole/1/2/7/64/1000 bytes, intervals 1024/1/3, async-iterable input and string chunks. The alignment guard and byte tail ensure unaligned subarrays, pooled Buffer.from(string) buffers and 1-byte splits pass; the lane-wise test is byte-order-agnostic, and a false negative only drops to the byte path.

history_reference.builds_on: round_2_planner_a (string-skip loop 4x unroll, sealed 1.499) and round_3_planner_a (WCLS outer skip, sealed 1.623). This plan stacks the u32 word reject on top of both merged changes.

This plan is the lower-variance alternative to swarU32 (round_3 idea 1, now remeasured at ~1.13x relative, sealed ~1.83): same u32 structure but simpler lane test, more predictable performance (1.06-1.11 vs 1.11-1.17), though lower ceiling (1.75 vs 1.83). Avoids viewU8, skipDef, quoteDirect, rej4n3 (all neutral/noise, round_4 brief idea 3).
